Data & Location

Last updated: 15 October 2026 [TO CONFIRM: effective date]

This page lists what the Yestermanac app reads from your device, what it sends over the network, and when. It describes the app as it is built today. Where a feature is not yet switched on, we say so.

Permissions the app asks for

Internet
To load pictures and use the online features listed below.
Notifications
For the daily events, holiday reminders and puzzle reminders you switch on. They are scheduled on your device.
Approximate location
Asked only when you tap “Use my location” (see below). The app never asks for precise location.

Android libraries used for scheduling may add standard background permissions, such as running scheduled work after a restart. [TO CONFIRM: final merged permission list of the release build]. The app does not ask for contacts, camera, microphone, files, accounts or an advertising ID.

What the app reads on your device

Language
Your device language chooses the language of the app and its content, unless you pick another one in Settings.
Country
Your country comes from your SIM card, then your mobile network, then your device's region setting. It sets your home country for events and public holidays. It stays on the device, except as part of a “The day you were born” lookup (below).
State or province
Used for regional holidays. You pick it from a list, or let the app find it with “Use my location”.
Time zone
Sets today's date and the almanac's default city. It stays on the device, except as part of a “The day you were born” lookup.
Date and time
The device clock decides which day's events you see and when notifications fire.

Location

  • No precise GPS. The app does not request Android's precise-location permission.
  • Approximate location only when you ask. There are two buttons: “Use my location to find my state/province” in Holiday reminders, and “Use my location” when choosing the place for the sky and almanac card. Only then does the app ask for approximate location.
  • How it is used. The app reads your device's last known approximate position, or asks Android for one. Android's built-in Geocoder turns it into a country, state or province, and place name. The Geocoder is part of Android, not Yestermanac; depending on your device it may send the position to Google's online services.
  • What is kept. For holiday reminders, only the state or province code you end up with. For the sky and almanac card, the coordinates rounded to 0.1° (about 11 km) and the place name, used to compute sunrise, sunset and the moon on your device. Both are saved in the app's settings, which are excluded from Android backup and device transfer (see the Privacy Policy).
  • Never at start-up or before a payment. The regional availability check (below) does not use your location, even while the permission is granted. Location is read only when you tap one of the two buttons above.
  • Yestermanac never sends your location to us. You can withdraw the permission at any time in Android settings and choose your region or city by hand instead.

Regional availability check

Because of sanctions law, the app checks your country when it starts and before a payment. It uses, in this order: your SIM country, your mobile network country, your device's region setting (only when there is no SIM or network country), and your time zone. It never uses your location. The result is used on the device and is not sent, except that a blocked start adds one anonymous “geo_blocked” count when usage counts are on and you have accepted the welcome screen.

What the app sends, and to whom

Pictures (Wikimedia)
When an entry has a picture, it is loaded from Wikimedia's servers (such as upload.wikimedia.org). They receive your IP address and an app identifier containing the app's name, version and our contact address, as Wikimedia's policy asks.
Wallet sign-in
When you tap “Connect”, your wallet app signs a sign-in message. Your public address stays on the device.
Seeker Genesis Token check
Your public wallet address is sent to a Solana RPC provider (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com) to check whether it holds a Seeker Genesis Token.
Pro payment and restore
The payment is a normal Solana transfer that you sign in your wallet. To prepare, send and confirm it, and to restore a purchase later, the app talks to Solana RPC providers (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com, then solana-rpc.publicnode.com) [TO CONFIRM: Helius fallback in the release build]. They receive your public address and IP address. The transfer itself is public on the blockchain.
Anonymous usage counts
One event name per request. The full list is: “app_open”, “terms_accepted”, “wallet_connected”, “wallet_disconnected”, “sgt_verified”, “sgt_not_found”, “payments_sol”, “payments_skr”, “purchases_restored”, “upgrade_viewed”, “settings_opened”, “geo_blocked”, “mix_saved”, “quiz_completed”, “share_card”, “search_used”, “sensitive_opened” and “born_lookup”. No ID, wallet address, date or typed text is included. Our server sees your IP address, as with any request, and derives your country from it. Nothing is counted, sent or queued before you accept the welcome screen; after that, counting is on by default and you can switch it off in Settings → Privacy. Events that cannot be sent wait on the device (up to 200) and are sent later. Not connected in the current build, so nothing is sent [TO CONFIRM: status at release].
Correction reports
When you use “Report a correction”: the entry ID, its language and your note (up to 1,000 characters, at most 5 reports a day). Reports wait on the device and are sent to the Yestermanac service only when it is connected; until then they stay queued. [TO CONFIRM: service live at release].
“The day you were born”
If the app is connected to the Yestermanac service, a lookup sends the date you look up (your full date of birth, or another date), the content language, your time zone, your home country and region, and display options. Like every request to the service, it carries a short-lived session that the app obtains with its random install identifier, so the service can apply each installation's daily limit. The app allows at most 30 new online lookups an hour. Without the service, the report is built on the device. The moon phase is always computed on the device. The usage count for this feature is the event name only, never the date. [TO CONFIRM: whether the release build is connected to the service].
Day content for languages without a bundled pack
English, Polish and Hungarian are bundled with the app and make no request for day content. For every other content language the app loads each day's entries from the Yestermanac service. A request contains only the date (month and day), the content language and the short-lived install session; no location is sent. Loaded days are kept on the device (the 60 most recently used days plus the days of your favourites), so they work offline afterwards, and once a day, on Wi-Fi only, the next day is loaded in advance. Offline with nothing kept yet, the English entries are shown and marked as such. A search in these languages sends your search words, the content language and a date. Holiday data for other years is not loaded from the service in this build. [TO CONFIRM: status at release].
Remote configuration
The app can fetch a signed settings document (prices, notices, regional list) from our configuration server. It sends no personal data beyond the normal request. Not connected in the current build. [TO CONFIRM: status at release].
Links you open
Source pages, Wikidata, further-reading sites (Grokipedia and Britannica only if you switch them on) and map locations open in your browser or maps app. The app does not fetch those sites itself.

What stays on your device

Notifications and widget
Scheduled and drawn on the device from the built-in content.
Sky and almanac
Sun and moon times are computed on the device.
Reading aloud
Uses the text-to-speech engine installed on your device. Depending on that engine, it may use its maker's online service.
Share cards
Drawn on the device. They leave it only when you choose an app in Android's share sheet.
Export
Calendar (.ics) and backup (.json) files are written only to a place you choose.
Your own dates and saved people
Kept in the app's storage. Saved people, dates of birth, your own dates and notes are all excluded from Android backup and device transfer.
